tagline: Mesas and longleaf pine, rugged by Louisiana standards.
intro: Forest Road 59 runs 17 miles across the Kisatchie National Forest, from Highway 117 at the ranger station on the west to Highway 119 on the east. The ground rises and falls between 80 and 400 feet above sea level, which is rugged by Louisiana standards, and mesas, buttes and sandstone outcrops show between the longleaf pines.

The government began buying this land in 1911, when much of it had been cut over by the timber companies. Caroline Dormon, a schoolteacher who went to work for the state forestry department, wrote letters and sat through meetings until a tract was chosen for protection in 1929, and she suggested the name Kisatchie.

moments.title: Longleaf Vista
moments.text: Four miles short of Highway 119, the vista looks out on three sides over the wilderness called the Little Grand Canyon, and a 1.5-mile loop climbs through meadows and hardwoods to high mesas.

moments.title: Kisatchie Hills Wilderness
moments.text: The wilderness can be entered only on foot or horseback, and anyone walking the whole 7-mile Backbone Trail has to wade the sand-bottomed Bayou Cypre, pronounced seep.

sources.label: Louisiana Office of Tourism, Longleaf Trail Byway (Wayback Machine snapshot)
